title: Quick repeat shipments
q: A *quick repeat* is a shipment that comes 7 days or less after the same customer's previous shipment. For every customer with at least one quick repeat, show CustomerID, CustomerName, QuickRepeats (how many) and ShortestGapDays (the smallest gap in days between two of their consecutive shipments). Sort by QuickRepeats descending, then ShortestGapDays, then CustomerID.
sql:
WITH e AS (
    SELECT CustomerID,
           DATEDIFF(day, LAG(ShipDate) OVER (PARTITION BY CustomerID ORDER BY ShipDate, ShipmentID), ShipDate) AS GapDays
    FROM retail_logistics.Shipments
)
SELECT p.CustomerID, p.CustomerName, COUNT(*) AS QuickRepeats, MIN(e.GapDays) AS ShortestGapDays
FROM e
JOIN retail_logistics.Customers AS p ON p.CustomerID = e.CustomerID
WHERE e.GapDays <= 7
GROUP BY p.CustomerID, p.CustomerName
ORDER BY QuickRepeats DESC, ShortestGapDays, p.CustomerID;
how: LAG(ShipDate) OVER (PARTITION BY CustomerID ORDER BY ShipDate) gives each row the previous date for the same customer. Compute the gap in a CTE first: a window function cannot go in WHERE.
a:
**Approach hint:** LAG(ShipDate) OVER (PARTITION BY CustomerID ORDER BY ShipDate) gives each row the previous date for the same customer. Compute the gap in a CTE first: a window function cannot go in WHERE.

title: Median vs average freight charge
q: Averages hide outliers. For each ShipmentCategory, show ShipmentCategory, Shipments (how many shipments), AverageValue, MedianValue and AboveMedian (AverageValue minus MedianValue), all money values rounded to 2 decimals. Use the FreightCharge column. Sort by ShipmentCategory.
sql:
WITH m AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT ShipmentCategory,
           COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY ShipmentCategory) AS Shipments,
           AVG(FreightCharge) OVER (PARTITION BY ShipmentCategory) AS AvgV,
           PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY FreightCharge) OVER (PARTITION BY ShipmentCategory) AS MedV
    FROM retail_logistics.Shipments
)
SELECT ShipmentCategory, Shipments,
       CAST(AvgV AS decimal(12,2)) AS AverageValue,
       CAST(MedV AS decimal(12,2)) AS MedianValue,
       CAST(AvgV - MedV AS decimal(12,2)) AS AboveMedian
FROM m
ORDER BY ShipmentCategory;
how: PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ...) OVER (PARTITION BY ...) returns the median on every row of the group; SELECT DISTINCT collapses it to one row per group. When the median is far below the average, a few large values pull the average up.
a:
**Approach hint:** PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ...) OVER (PARTITION BY ...) returns the median on every row of the group; SELECT DISTINCT collapses it to one row per group. When the median is far below the average, a few large values pull the average up.

title: Month-to-date running total
q: For Closed shipments only, show each ShipDate with DayTotal (the sum of FreightCharge that day) and MonthToDate: the running total that starts again on the first day of each month. Sort by ShipDate.
sql:
WITH d AS (
    SELECT ShipDate, SUM(FreightCharge) AS DayTotal
    FROM retail_logistics.Shipments
    WHERE Status = 'Closed'
    GROUP BY ShipDate
)
SELECT ShipDate, DayTotal,
       SUM(DayTotal) OVER (PARTITION BY YEAR(ShipDate), MONTH(ShipDate)
                           ORDER BY ShipDate ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS MonthToDate
FROM d
ORDER BY ShipDate;
how: Aggregate to one row per day first, then SUM() OVER (PARTITION BY year and month ORDER BY date). The PARTITION BY is what makes the total restart each month.

title: The customers behind half of all value
q: Rank customers by their total freight charge (all shipments). Show the smallest group of top customers that together make up at least 50% of the grand total: CustomerID, CustomerName, Total and CumulativePct (their running share of the grand total, 2 decimals). Break ties in Total by CustomerID. Sort by Total descending, then CustomerID.
sql:
WITH t AS (
    SELECT CustomerID, SUM(FreightCharge) AS Total
    FROM retail_logistics.Shipments
    GROUP BY CustomerID
), r AS (
    SELECT CustomerID, Total,
           SUM(Total) OVER (ORDER BY Total DESC, CustomerID ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS Running,
           SUM(Total) OVER () AS Grand
    FROM t
)
SELECT r.CustomerID, p.CustomerName, r.Total, CAST(100.0 * r.Running / r.Grand AS decimal(5,2)) AS CumulativePct
FROM r
JOIN retail_logistics.Customers AS p ON p.CustomerID = r.CustomerID
WHERE r.Running - r.Total < 0.5 * r.Grand
ORDER BY r.Total DESC, r.CustomerID;
how: Total per group, then a running SUM() OVER (ORDER BY Total DESC). Keep a row while the running total *before* it (Running minus Total) is still under half: that includes the row that crosses the line.
a:
**Approach hint:** Total per group, then a running SUM() OVER (ORDER BY Total DESC). Keep a row while the running total *before* it (Running minus Total) is still under half: that includes the row that crosses the line.

title: On-time delivery rate per carrier
q: A package is on time when its Delivered scan happens on or before its PromisedDate. For each carrier show CarrierName, ServiceLevel, Delivered (packages with a Delivered scan), OnTime and OnTimePct (2 decimals). Only carriers with at least 5 delivered packages. Sort by OnTimePct, then CarrierName.
sql:
WITH d AS (
    SELECT PackageID, MIN(ScanTime) AS DeliveredAt
    FROM retail_logistics.TrackingEvents
    WHERE EventStatus = 'Delivered'
    GROUP BY PackageID
)
SELECT c.CarrierName, c.ServiceLevel, COUNT(*) AS Delivered,
       SUM(CASE WHEN CAST(d.DeliveredAt AS date) <= pk.PromisedDate THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS OnTime,
       CAST(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN CAST(d.DeliveredAt AS date) <= pk.PromisedDate THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) AS decimal(5,2)) AS OnTimePct
FROM d
JOIN retail_logistics.ShipmentPackages AS pk ON pk.PackageID = d.PackageID
JOIN retail_logistics.Shipments AS s ON s.ShipmentID = pk.ShipmentID
JOIN retail_logistics.Carriers AS c ON c.CarrierID = s.CarrierID
GROUP BY c.CarrierID, c.CarrierName, c.ServiceLevel
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5
ORDER BY OnTimePct, c.CarrierName;
how: Get one delivered time per package first. ScanTime has a time part and PromisedDate does not: compare dates (CAST AS date), or a delivery at 10:00 on the promised day looks late.
a:

title: Packages that never arrived
q: List packages that have a PickedUp scan but no Delivered scan. Show TrackingNumber, CustomerName, PromisedDate, LastStatus (EventStatus of the latest scan), LastScan (its ScanTime) and LastLocation. Sort by PromisedDate, then TrackingNumber.
sql:
WITH last AS (
    SELECT PackageID, EventStatus, ScanTime, LocationName,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY PackageID ORDER BY ScanTime DESC, TrackingEventID DESC) AS rn
    FROM retail_logistics.TrackingEvents
)
SELECT pk.TrackingNumber, cu.CustomerName, pk.PromisedDate,
       l.EventStatus AS LastStatus, l.ScanTime AS LastScan, l.LocationName AS LastLocation
FROM retail_logistics.ShipmentPackages AS pk
JOIN retail_logistics.Shipments AS s ON s.ShipmentID = pk.ShipmentID
JOIN retail_logistics.Customers AS cu ON cu.CustomerID = s.CustomerID
JOIN last AS l ON l.PackageID = pk.PackageID AND l.rn = 1
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM retail_logistics.TrackingEvents AS t WHERE t.PackageID = pk.PackageID AND t.EventStatus = 'PickedUp')
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM retail_logistics.TrackingEvents AS t WHERE t.PackageID = pk.PackageID AND t.EventStatus = 'Delivered')
ORDER BY pk.PromisedDate, pk.TrackingNumber;
how: EXISTS for 'has this scan', NOT EXISTS for 'has no such scan'. The latest scan per package is ROW_NUMBER() ... ORDER BY ScanTime DESC = 1.
a:
**Approach hint:** EXISTS for 'has this scan', NOT EXISTS for 'has no such scan'. The latest scan per package is ROW_NUMBER() ... ORDER BY ScanTime DESC = 1.

title: Value tiers with NTILE
q: Split the customers that have shipments into 4 equal-sized tiers by total FreightCharge with NTILE(4), tier 1 = highest (ties broken by CustomerID). For each tier show Tier, Customers (how many), MinTotal, MaxTotal, TierTotal and ShareOfAllPct (the tier's share of the grand total, 2 decimals). Sort by Tier.
sql:
WITH t AS (
    SELECT CustomerID, SUM(FreightCharge) AS Total
    FROM retail_logistics.Shipments
    GROUP BY CustomerID
), n AS (
    SELECT CustomerID, Total, NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY Total DESC, CustomerID) AS Tier
    FROM t
)
SELECT Tier, COUNT(*) AS Customers, MIN(Total) AS MinTotal, MAX(Total) AS MaxTotal, SUM(Total) AS TierTotal,
       CAST(100.0 * SUM(Total) / SUM(SUM(Total)) OVER () AS decimal(5,2)) AS ShareOfAllPct
FROM n
GROUP BY Tier
ORDER BY Tier;
how: NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY ...) deals rows into 4 buckets. After GROUP BY Tier, SUM(SUM(Total)) OVER () is the grand total across all tiers, so the share needs no second query.
a:
**Approach hint:** NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY ...) deals rows into 4 buckets. After GROUP BY Tier, SUM(SUM(Total)) OVER () is the grand total across all tiers, so the share needs no second query.

title: Pickup-to-delivery hours by service level
q: For each delivered package, measure hours from its first PickedUp scan to its first Delivered scan. Per carrier ServiceLevel show Packages, AvgHours, MedianHours and MaxHours (all to 1 decimal). Sort by AvgHours.
sql:
WITH p AS (
    SELECT t.PackageID,
           MIN(CASE WHEN t.EventStatus = 'PickedUp' THEN t.ScanTime END) AS PickedUp,
           MIN(CASE WHEN t.EventStatus = 'Delivered' THEN t.ScanTime END) AS Delivered
    FROM retail_logistics.TrackingEvents AS t
    GROUP BY t.PackageID
), h AS (
    SELECT c.ServiceLevel, DATEDIFF(minute, p.PickedUp, p.Delivered) / 60.0 AS Hours
    FROM p
    JOIN retail_logistics.ShipmentPackages AS pk ON pk.PackageID = p.PackageID
    JOIN retail_logistics.Shipments AS s ON s.ShipmentID = pk.ShipmentID
    JOIN retail_logistics.Carriers AS c ON c.CarrierID = s.CarrierID
    WHERE p.PickedUp IS NOT NULL AND p.Delivered IS NOT NULL
), m AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT ServiceLevel,
           COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY ServiceLevel) AS Packages,
           AVG(Hours) OVER (PARTITION BY ServiceLevel) AS AvgH,
           PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY Hours) OVER (PARTITION BY ServiceLevel) AS MedH,
           MAX(Hours) OVER (PARTITION BY ServiceLevel) AS MaxH
    FROM h
)
SELECT ServiceLevel, Packages, CAST(AvgH AS decimal(8,1)) AS AvgHours,
       CAST(MedH AS decimal(8,1)) AS MedianHours, CAST(MaxH AS decimal(8,1)) AS MaxHours
FROM m
ORDER BY AvgHours;

title: Late deliveries in a customer's first 60 days
q: For customers whose first shipment was in the first half of 2024 (January to June), look only at packages on their shipments dispatched within 60 days of that first shipment. Show CustomerID, CustomerName, Packages, Late (Delivered scan after PromisedDate, or no Delivered scan at all) and LatePct (2 decimals), for customers with at least one late package. Sort by LatePct descending, then CustomerID.
sql:
WITH f AS (
    SELECT CustomerID, MIN(ShipDate) AS FirstShip
    FROM retail_logistics.Shipments
    GROUP BY CustomerID
    HAVING MIN(ShipDate) >= '2024-01-01' AND MIN(ShipDate) < '2024-07-01'
), d AS (
    SELECT PackageID, MIN(ScanTime) AS DeliveredAt
    FROM retail_logistics.TrackingEvents
    WHERE EventStatus = 'Delivered'
    GROUP BY PackageID
), p AS (
    SELECT s.CustomerID,
           CASE WHEN d.DeliveredAt IS NULL OR CAST(d.DeliveredAt AS date) > pk.PromisedDate THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS IsLate
    FROM f
    JOIN retail_logistics.Shipments AS s ON s.CustomerID = f.CustomerID
         AND s.ShipDate <= DATEADD(day, 60, f.FirstShip)
    JOIN retail_logistics.ShipmentPackages AS pk ON pk.ShipmentID = s.ShipmentID
    LEFT JOIN d ON d.PackageID = pk.PackageID
)
SELECT p.CustomerID, c.CustomerName, COUNT(*) AS Packages, SUM(p.IsLate) AS Late,
       CAST(100.0 * SUM(p.IsLate) / COUNT(*) AS decimal(5,2)) AS LatePct
FROM p
JOIN retail_logistics.Customers AS c ON c.CustomerID = p.CustomerID
GROUP BY p.CustomerID, c.CustomerName
HAVING SUM(p.IsLate) > 0
ORDER BY LatePct DESC, p.CustomerID;
how: Three steps: each customer's first date (filtered in HAVING), the shipments inside their 60-day window (a join condition relative to that date), then a late flag per package. Missing delivery counts as late, so LEFT JOIN the delivery scans.
a:
**Approach hint:** Three steps: each customer's first date (filtered in HAVING), the shipments inside their 60-day window (a join condition relative to that date), then a late flag per package. Missing delivery counts as late, so LEFT JOIN the delivery scans.

title: Longest quiet period per region
q: For each Region (from Customers), find the longest stretch with no shipments at all between two consecutive shipment dates in that region. Show Region, GapStart (the last date before the gap), GapEnd (the next date) and DaysWithout. If two gaps tie for longest in a region, show both. Sort by DaysWithout descending, then Region, then GapStart.
sql:
WITH d AS (
    SELECT p.Region, e.ShipDate AS GapEnd,
           LAG(e.ShipDate) OVER (PARTITION BY p.Region ORDER BY e.ShipDate, e.ShipmentID) AS GapStart
    FROM retail_logistics.Shipments AS e
    JOIN retail_logistics.Customers AS p ON p.CustomerID = e.CustomerID
), r AS (
    SELECT Region, GapStart, GapEnd, DATEDIFF(day, GapStart, GapEnd) AS DaysWithout,
           RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY Region ORDER BY DATEDIFF(day, GapStart, GapEnd) DESC) AS rk
    FROM d
    WHERE GapStart IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT Region, GapStart, GapEnd, DaysWithout
FROM r
WHERE rk = 1
ORDER BY DaysWithout DESC, Region, GapStart;
how: LAG over the region's dates gives the previous date; DATEDIFF gives the gap. RANK() (not ROW_NUMBER) keeps ties for the top spot.
a:
**Approach hint:** LAG over the region's dates gives the previous date; DATEDIFF gives the gap. RANK() (not ROW_NUMBER) keeps ties for the top spot.
